rationale: Round 0 built and passed cleanly, so this round escalates obfuscation intensity. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain weight because sha_transform is dominated by word-level arithmetic (rotations, adds, XOR/AND/OR mixes) where instruction substitution destroys the recognizable SHA-1 round pattern at negligible correctness risk. BCF and IBR are raised next: sha_transform's four 80-iteration round loops and byte_reverse's byte-loop tolerate bogus control flow and opaque-predicate branching well, and the reference binary's small text size (1832 bytes) leaves ample size headroom. FLA is kept moderate — flattening sha_stream/sha_update's outer loops hinders tracing, but its dispatch overhead lands on the hottest code, so RuntimeCost is non-trivial. SPLIT stays a cheap diversity amplifier on the larger function bodies. ICALL and IGV are enabled but conservative: indirect calls obscure sha_transform's call sites yet carry the highest miscompilation risk on fixed prototype code, and IGV's encoded globals must preserve the exact K-table constants, so their CorrectnessRisk weights gate selection to functions where the feature model is confident. Overall the table biases toward arithmetic and control-flow transformation (SUB/BCF/IBR) that this workload's feature profile favors, while size and runtime costs are kept below the correctness-critical thresholds that round 0 already demonstrated are safe.
